# Document extraction fixtures

These fixtures support ticket #33's deterministic PDF and DOCX extraction
tests. All visible content, metadata, and malformed payloads were authored for
CogniStore. The DOCX package scaffold comes from python-docx's MIT-licensed
default template; its notice is retained in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES).

## Expected valid-document output

`sample.pdf` and `sample.docx` contain the same three logical text blocks. After
whitespace normalization, both must yield this exact string (single line-feed
characters between blocks and no trailing line feed):

```text
CogniStore Document Fixture
This project-authored sample verifies deterministic text extraction.
Alpha records stay searchable. Beta pages remain reproducible.
```

Both files intentionally share these core metadata values:

| Field | Expected value |
| --- | --- |
| title | `CogniStore Document Fixture` |
| author | `CogniStore Contributors` |
| subject | `Licensed deterministic extraction fixture` |
| keywords | `cognistore, extraction, fixture` |
| created | `2000-01-01T00:00:00Z` |
| modified | `2000-01-01T00:00:00Z` |

The PDF is one page and sets both `creator` and `producer` to
`CogniStore fixture generator`. The DOCX sets `last_modified_by` to that value,
`category` to `Test Fixture`, `revision` to `1`, and `language` to `en-US`.

## Negative fixtures

| File | Intended result |
| --- | --- |
| `encrypted.pdf` | Reject as encrypted without attempting password recovery. Its validation-only password is `fixture-password`. |
| `corrupt.pdf` | Reject as a truncated PDF. |
| `corrupt.docx` | Reject as an OOXML-like ZIP whose main document XML is truncated. |
| `unsupported.txt` | Reject as an unsupported document format. |

Failures from these files must remain scoped to the individual object so that
unrelated indexing work can continue.

## Reproduction and provenance

The binary fixtures are generated by `generate.py` using deterministic PDF and
ZIP settings. From this directory, run:

```shell
python generate.py
```

The checked-in binaries were generated with Python 3.12, `python-docx` 1.2.0,
`pypdf` 6.10.0, and `reportlab` 4.4.9. The script uses RC4-128 only to create a
small broadly readable encrypted-test artifact; it is not an example of a
recommended encryption choice.
